chains.title: GABPA binds the C228T alt allele and activates TERT in glioblastoma

links.claim: GABPA binds the alt A allele more strongly than the ref G allele at chr5:1295113. GABPA's own QBiC-SELEX model shows an alt increase (effect +4.01, z 68.47), and additional Ets models show the same direction. GABPA ChIP-seq peaks over the variant are reported in HepG2/SK-N-SH, and literature reports GABPA/GABPB1 activation of the mutant TERT promoter in glioblastoma. Direct GABPA occupancy in a glioblastoma biosample is still not shown in the provided ENCODE data.
The variant lies in promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 within the TERT promoter, an active promoter element.
This promoter element is at the TERT TSS (0.0 kb upstream; TERT upstream_gene_variant).
Glioblastoma is the relevant context: GABPA is expressed in DepMap glioblastoma lines (15.52 TPM), and literature places GABPA/GABPB1 at the mutant TERT promoter in glioblastoma.

GABPA/GABPB1 activation of the mutant TERT promoter increases telomerase; GABPA depletion or GABPB1 knockdown inhibits telomerase and tumorigenic potential of glioblastoma cells, and TERT promoter mutations mark poor prognosis.

predictions: Allele-specific GABPA ChIP in glioblastoma cells should show higher GABPA occupancy on the alt allele.
TERT mRNA or telomerase activity should be higher on the alt allele, and GABPA knockdown should reduce alt-driven TERT expression.
A GABPA ChIP-seq peak over chr5:1295113 should be detectable in matching glioblastoma biosamples.
falsified_if: GABPA binding at this base is not allele-specific in glioblastoma cells.
The alt allele does not increase TERT expression, or the effect persists after GABPA depletion.
GABPA is not expressed or cannot occupy the TERT promoter in the relevant glioblastoma context.

chains.title: No TF-mediated allelic effect at this base
predictions: There is no allele-specific TF occupancy or allele-specific reporter activity at chr5:1295113 in the relevant cells.
Any TERT association is due to a linked causal variant, a passenger mutation, or another mechanism not mediated by a TF binding this base.
TERT expression is not allele-specific at this position in glioblastoma cells.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GABPA or another Ets-factor binding at chr5:1295113 is demonstrated in glioblastoma cells.
The alt allele increases TERT expression in an allele-specific reporter assay, and the effect is abolished by mutating the TF site or depleting the TF.

chains.title: CTCF binds the ref allele more strongly and loss of a repressive CTCF site on the alt allele derepresses TERT

links.claim: CTCF binds the ref G allele more strongly than the alt A allele; the CTCF own QBiC-SELEX model shows ref preference (z -14.7, effect -1.719). The only ENCODE CTCF peak over this variant is in DOHH2, not glioblastoma.
The variant lies in promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 in the TERT promoter.
The element is immediately upstream of TERT, 0 kb from the TSS.
CTCF is expressed in glioblastoma DepMap lines (26.45 TPM), but CTCF occupancy at this promoter in glioblastoma is not shown.
If CTCF repressed TERT at this promoter, reduced CTCF binding on the alt allele could derepress TERT and promote disease; there is no direct evidence for CTCF repression here.

predictions: CTCF ChIP should show higher ref-allele occupancy at chr5:1295113 in a cell type where CTCF binds this promoter.
If CTCF is repressive, the alt allele should increase TERT expression when CTCF is present.
CTCF knockdown or mutation of the CTCF site should mimic the alt allele.
falsified_if: CTCF does not occupy the TERT promoter in glioblastoma cells.
CTCF binding is not allele-specific at this base.
CTCF acts as an activator rather than a repressor at this promoter, reversing the predicted direction.

chains.title: ETV3, another Ets factor, binds the alt allele and activates TERT

links.claim: ETV3 is a candidate Ets factor that would bind the alt A allele more strongly, based on a CIS-BP-mapped ETV5 Ets model (z 166.19, effect 2.121 alt). ETV3 has no ENCODE ChIP occupancy over this variant, and the mapped model is shared with other Ets factors, so this is weak and cannot distinguish ETV3 from GABPA.
The variant lies in promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 in the TERT promoter.
The element is 0 kb from the TERT TSS and is annotated as a TERT upstream promoter variant.
ETV3 is expressed at low level in glioblastoma DepMap lines (8.69 TPM), but no occupancy or TERT-promoter activity is shown in this context.
If ETV3 occupied the alt allele, increased ETV3-driven TERT transcription could contribute to disease; this is speculative because occupancy is not shown.

predictions: ETV3 ChIP in glioblastoma cells should show allele-specific occupancy at chr5:1295113.
ETV3 knockdown should reduce alt-driven TERT expression if this chain is correct.
The alt allele should increase ETV3-dependent reporter activity through the Ets motif.
falsified_if: ETV3 does not occupy the TERT promoter in glioblastoma cells.
ETV3 depletion does not affect TERT expression from the alt allele.
The allelic effect is fully explained by GABPA rather than ETV3.

chains.title: TFAP2A binds the ref allele more strongly and loss of TFAP2A binding on the alt allele increases TERT

links.claim: TFAP2A binds the ref G allele more strongly than the alt A allele; a CIS-BP-mapped TFAP2E AP-2 model shows ref preference (z -36.84, effect -1.289). TFAP2A occupancy over this variant is not shown, and the mapped model is shared with TFAP2C.
The variant lies in promoter-like cCRE EH38E3622530 in the TERT promoter.
The element is 0 kb from the TERT TSS.
TFAP2A is expressed in glioblastoma DepMap lines (9.65 TPM), but its occupancy at this promoter is not established.
If TFAP2A repressed TERT, alt-mediated loss of TFAP2A binding could increase TERT expression and contribute to disease; this is speculative without occupancy data.

predictions: TFAP2A ChIP should show ref-allele-preferential binding at chr5:1295113 if it occupies this site.
The alt allele should increase TERT expression if TFAP2A is a repressor at this promoter.
TFAP2A knockdown should increase TERT expression from the ref allele.
falsified_if: TFAP2A does not occupy the TERT promoter in glioblastoma cells.
TFAP2A binding is not allele-specific at this base.
TFAP2A activates rather than represses TERT, reversing the predicted direction.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr5:1295113:G>A, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap subtype median Glioblastoma), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 20 occupied (15 with a strong site), 5 of 111 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 0 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 552 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 1 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.

Telomere length maintenance, critical for cancer progression, can be driven by TERT promoter mutations (TERTp MUT ), which are markers of poor prognosis across multiple cancers.

Here, we identified previously uncharacterized pathways regulating TERTp MUT activity by inserting a luciferase reporter downstream of TERTp MUT in SW1736 anaplastic thyroid cancer cells via CRISPR-Cas9, generating SW1736TERT/LUC, and screening a 218-kinase inhibitor library.

TERT promoter mutations occur in the majority of glioblastoma, bladder cancer (BC), and other malignancies while the ETS family transcription factors GABPA and its partner GABPB1 activate the mutant TERT promoter and telomerase in these tumors.
GABPA depletion or the disruption of the GABPA/GABPB1 complex by knocking down GABPB1 was shown to inhibit telomerase, thereby eliminating the tumorigenic potential of glioblastoma cells.

In this review article, we summarize critical mechanisms activating TERT transcription, with special emphases on the contribution of TERT promoter mutations and structural alterations at the TERT locus, and briefly discuss the underlying implications of these genomic events-driven TERT hyperactivity in cancer initiation/progression and potential clinical applications as well.
